feature: Assessment Monitoring / weekly-rescan surface (Git #454, area:shane-mccaw-consulting) — access gate, real testbed rescan trigger, and the real weekly cron cadence. Written to be honest about the gap between the requested framing ('weekly re-scan gated behind a signed SOW') and what actually exists in code (see notes).
notes: PROVENANCE / GIT #454. This manifest was written after a full source investigation of the 'Assessment Monitoring' product. The requested framing was: a weekly re-scan GATED BEHIND A SIGNED SOW, with a real scheduled trigger and a signed-SOW gate that blocks unentitled customers. GROUND TRUTH after reading the code: that exact feature — a weekly rescan whose gate is a *signed SOW* — DOES NOT EXIST as one unified mechanism. Rather than fabricate coverage for a gate/trigger that isn't there (which would violate this repo's test-honesty discipline), this manifest asserts the REAL, adjacent mechanisms that DO exist and documents each divergence in-line below. Sources read: seed-system-workflows.ts (the weekly cron workflow), workflow-executor.ts (triggerScheduledWorkflows + computeNextCronRun), sow-expiry-sweep.ts, portal-assessment.ts (debug-trigger-scan), diagnostics-runner.ts (runDiagnostics), portal-customer-engines.ts (the payment entitlement gate), sow-monitoring-addon.ts (pricing resolver), journeyPreviewFixture.ts (the 'tenant-monitoring' design fixture), admin-workflows.ts (the trigger-inspection endpoints), requireAuth.ts (the guards).

DIVERGENCE 1 — THE 'SIGNED-SOW GATE' DOES NOT EXIST. There is no code of the form `if (!sow.signed) return 403` in front of any rescan or monitoring read. The gates that genuinely exist are: (a) the manual customer-reachable rescan trigger POST /api/portal/assessment/debug-trigger-scan is hard-gated to TESTBED tenants (portal-assessment.ts: `customer.isTestbed !== true` -> 403 'Scan trigger is not available for this account'); (b) raw findings/recommendation TEXT on GET /api/portal/dashboard is gated on PAYMENT, not signature — `assessment_sow_agreements.status IN ('paid','free_activated')` (portal-customer-engines.ts isPaidTier); composite/pillar SCORES are never gated. So a customer 'without a signed SOW' is not the real access boundary — the real boundaries are testbed-flag (for the manual trigger), payment status (for findings text), and role/auth (for every portal + admin route). This manifest asserts the boundaries that are real and deterministic with the available testbed credentials.

DIVERGENCE 2 — THE WEEKLY CADENCE IS REAL, BUT TIER+CONSENT GATED, NOT SOW GATED. A genuine weekly schedule-triggered rescan EXISTS: the seeded Workflow-Engine definition '__system__: Weekly Retargeting Rescan — Free/Assessment Tenants' (seed-system-workflows.ts), triggerType 'schedule', cron '0 3 * * 1' (every Monday 03:00). It is dispatched by triggerScheduledWorkflows() (index.ts setInterval 60s -> workflow-executor.ts, which reschedules via computeNextCronRun and stamps wf_triggers.next_run_at). Its fan-out selects `users.msp_role IN ('Free','Assessment')` whose tenant Graph consent is 'granted' — and its OWN code comment says: 'Explicitly NOT a Monitoring subscription — does not touch msp_subscriptions or any billing/monitoring_tier config.' So the real cadence is gated on tenant TIER + Graph CONSENT, and is deliberately independent of any purchased/signed monitoring product. The CADENCE apiTests below assert this real definition + cron via the admin trigger-inspection endpoint.

DIVERGENCE 3 — 'TENANT MONITORING' IS A PRICED SOW ADD-ON LINE ITEM, NOT A RUNNING HOURLY ENGINE. The 'Six signal engines against your tenant every hour' copy (journeyPreviewFixture.ts / sow-monitoring-addon.ts) is self-documented IN THE CODE as marketing shorthand ('this is marketing shorthand, not a literal per-tier engine count'). resolveTenantMonitoringAddon() is a per-seat PRICING resolver over `services` rows (serviceType 'monitoring_tier'); it contains no entitlement/gate logic and fires no scan. There is no six-engine hourly rescan wired to a purchased monitoring SOW. Nothing here asserts an hourly-six-engine loop because none exists.

DIVERGENCE 4 — RESOLVED under Git #1059. The #454 dashboard drift visualization described below as unbuilt now exists: a new GET /api/portal/assessment/history route (portal-assessment.ts) returns the customer's real tenant_monitor_profiles rows (checkKey/status/severityMatched/collectedAt) for a trailing 12-week window, additively fetched by assessment-dashboard.tsx (the pre-existing single-snapshot fetch is untouched) and rendered by a new AssessmentDriftChart.tsx (artifacts/msp-portal/src/components/charts/). Pillar grouping happens CLIENT-SIDE via warRoomPillarForCheckKey (warRoomScan.ts's WAR_ROOM_PILLAR_DOMAINS) — the server route deliberately returns raw rows, same discipline /portal/scan-plan already documents. Score per pillar per real rescan day is the % of that pillar's checks with status 'ok' that day — a real derivation, not a fabricated number. See DIVERGENCE 4B below for the apiTests/uiSteps added for this and the real-data honesty caveat.

DIVERGENCE 4B — #1059's DRIFT CHART DATA STATE IS NOT YET KNOWN/DETERMINISTIC. The weekly Copilot Assessment rescan (#1058) only just went live, so at the time #1059 was written most/all tenants — including the testbed account this manifest drives — have very few or zero real tenant_monitor_profiles rows yet. AssessmentDriftChart.tsx therefore has THREE mutually-exclusive real render states, each with its own data-testid: `assessment-drift-empty` (zero history rows), `assessment-drift-sparse` (fewer than 2 real rescan days, or no check maps to any pillar), `assessment-drift-chart` (>=2 real rescan days with pillar-mapped data — the actual chart renders). Which one is true for the testbed tenant right now cannot be predicted from source alone, so the uiStep below asserts elementwise OR across all three testids (a single CSS selector listing all three, comma-separated) rather than guessing one and risking a false red — the same honesty discipline this manifest already applies to the SOW-gate divergence above. The apiTests below assert the endpoint's real, count-independent contract (200 + points is an array) regardless of how many rows exist.

WHAT A RE-SCAN ACTUALLY PRODUCES: all scan paths converge on runDiagnostics() (diagnostics-runner.ts), which INSERTS an msp_diagnostic_runs row (status pending -> running -> completed/failed/partial, with startedAt/completedAt) and writes findings rows, then emits a 'diagnostics.run_completed' workflow event. There is NO nextScanAt / scan_cadence / monitoring_enabled column anywhere; 'lastScanAt' shown in the portal is DERIVED from the most-recent completed run row. The RESCAN apiTests below assert the trigger creates a real, persisted, active run (runId + backend-computed checksTotal). ASYNC LIMIT (same as money-path-e2e.json / remediation-tracker-e2e.json): debug-trigger-scan returns 202 immediately and runDiagnostics runs in the background; the executor cannot await completion, so the post-scan score/finding DELTA ('genuinely updated results') is asserted at the trigger + persisted-active-run level, and the completed-scan delta is a polling follow-up for when the runner grows a poll primitive (cf. #877). Firing the trigger twice proves a fresh run row is minted each call (each returns its own new runId).

TESTBED-ONLY / DEV-ORIGIN-ONLY SAFETY: this manifest never touches raw DB and performs no real M365 Graph writes. The only write it causes is debug-trigger-scan inserting an msp_diagnostic_runs row on the TESTBED tenant — additive read-only-scan telemetry on a testbed account, identical to what money-path-e2e.json and remediation-tracker-e2e.json already leave, so no teardown is required. The manual trigger is server-side hard-gated to testbed tenants (202 only for a genuinely testbed-flagged account — a 202 here also PROVES the account is testbed-flagged, not merely asserted client-side). Run against the .replit.dev dev origin (same origin the other copilot-readiness manifests target).

ENV VARS required in BuildConsole -> Settings -> Test Environment Variables: DEPLOY_URL (the .replit.dev dev origin serving /api). TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD (the designated TESTBED Assessment-role account — same account money-path-e2e.json + remediation-tracker-e2e.json drive; it must be isTestbed=true or the RESCAN block's 202 becomes a 403). SECRET_KEY (= BUILD_TRACKER_INGEST_TOKEN) — used ONLY to prove the strict admin surface REJECTS it. TEST_ADMIN_EMAIL / TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD (a role='admin' account) — REQUIRED for the CADENCE block, because GET /api/admin/workflows/triggers is guarded by requireAdmin (strict: req.user.role==='admin'), which — unlike the requireAdminOrIngestToken testbed endpoints — does NOT honor the ingest token (requireAuth.ts:158,183). If TEST_ADMIN_EMAIL/PASSWORD are not provisioned, the admin login returns 401, {{adminToken}} stays unset, and every CADENCE step fails LOUDLY (by design — that failure means 'provision a testbed admin account', it is not a false negative about the cron). This is the manifest's one Shane To-Do.

AUTH-BOUNDARY FACTS asserted below (all real, all deterministic with the creds above): (1) anonymous (no bearer) -> 401 on the trigger, the scan-status read, and the SOW read (requireRole/requireAuth). (2) valid Assessment-role bearer -> 403 on the admin trigger-config surface (requireAdmin, wrong role). (3) the ingest token (SECRET_KEY) -> 401 on the admin trigger-config surface (requireAdmin runs requireAuth first and the ingest token is not a valid JWT) — proving the workflow-config surface is strictly admin-gated, NOT ingest-openable like the testbed reset endpoints. These three together are the honest, real answer to 'a caller without the right entitlement cannot trigger/read monitoring' — the entitlement that matters is testbed-flag + role + auth, not a signed SOW.

apiTests.name: SETUP 1/2 — log in as the designated TESTBED Assessment account; extract the bearer used by the GATE + RESCAN blocks. (Same account money-path-e2e.json / remediation-tracker-e2e.json drive.)

SETUP 2/2 — log in as the TESTBED ADMIN account (role='admin') for the CADENCE block's requireAdmin-guarded trigger-inspection endpoint; extract {{adminToken}}. PRECONDITION: needs TEST_ADMIN_EMAIL/PASSWORD provisioned (the one Shane To-Do). If unset, this 401s and the CADENCE steps fail loudly — that is the signal to provision the account, not a cron regression.

GATE A1 — anonymous (no bearer) cannot trigger a rescan: POST debug-trigger-scan without Authorization is refused by requireRole('Assessment') -> 401. The rescan trigger is genuinely access-gated, not open.
GATE A2 — anonymous cannot read scan status: GET /portal/scan-status without a bearer -> 401.
GATE A3 — anonymous cannot read the SOW/monitoring scope: GET /portal/assessment/sow without a bearer -> 401 (requireRole('Assessment')).

GATE A4 — WRONG ROLE is genuinely blocked from the monitoring-schedule CONFIG surface: a valid Assessment-role bearer hitting the admin trigger-inspection endpoint is refused by requireAdmin -> 403. (Proves the cron/monitoring configuration is not reachable by an ordinary customer, only an admin.)

GATE A5 — the INGEST TOKEN is NOT admin: SECRET_KEY (BUILD_TRACKER_INGEST_TOKEN) on the requireAdmin-guarded trigger surface -> 401 (requireAdmin runs requireAuth first; the ingest token is not a valid JWT). This is the real boundary between the strict admin surface and the requireAdminOrIngestToken testbed endpoints — the workflow-config surface is admin-only, not ingest-openable.

RESCAN B1 — a genuinely testbed-flagged Assessment account CAN trigger the real rescan: POST debug-trigger-scan -> 202 with a fresh runId. runDiagnostics runs async; a 202 also proves the account passed the hard server-side isTestbed gate (a non-testbed tenant would 403 here). Extract the run id.
RESCAN B2 — the trigger reports the pending status contract on the wire (real 202 envelope, not a mocked 200).
RESCAN B3 — the rescan produced a REAL, PERSISTED active run: scan-status now reports active.runId (the run row genuinely landed in msp_diagnostic_runs, not a static/mocked response).

RESCAN B4 — the active run carries a real backend-computed checksTotal (the count runDiagnostics computes over the monitoring package), evidence the scan is doing genuine work, not returning an empty placeholder. NOTE: the completed-scan score/finding DELTA is async and not awaitable here (see the ASYNC LIMIT note) — this asserts a real in-progress run, which is the honest maximum for this runner.
RESCAN B5 — the maintained-scan surface the drift/report layer reads is live: GET /portal/assessment/status returns a real copilotGate on the wire (same payload the Documents/dashboard hooks poll).

DRIFT D1 (#1059) — anonymous (no bearer) cannot read weekly-rescan history: GET /portal/assessment/history without Authorization -> 401 (requireRole('Assessment'), same guard as the other Assessment routes above).

DRIFT D2 (#1059) — the real history endpoint returns its raw-points contract: 200 with $.points as an array. Count-independent on purpose (see DIVERGENCE 4B) — zero, one, or many real rows are all a valid, honest response this early after #1058 went live.

CADENCE C1 — the real weekly rescan cadence EXISTS as a Workflow-Engine schedule trigger: GET /admin/workflows/triggers (admin bearer) returns the seeded '__system__: Weekly Retargeting Rescan — Free/Assessment Tenants' definition on the wire. containsAny substring-matches the definition name in the real triggers list.

CADENCE C2 — the cadence is genuinely WEEKLY: the same triggers list carries the real cron expression '0 3 * * 1' (every Monday 03:00) for a schedule-type trigger. This is the real scheduling logic, on the wire, not a fixture.

CADENCE C3 — the trigger is a SCHEDULE trigger and is ENABLED (the 60s triggerScheduledWorkflows scanner only fires enabled schedule triggers whose next_run_at has passed). containsAny confirms a real 'schedule' trigger type is present in the list.

CADENCE C4 — the cadence logic has actually COMPUTED a next fire: the triggers list carries a nextRunAt field (computeNextCronRun stamps wf_triggers.next_run_at each reschedule). Presence of the nextRunAt key on the wire confirms the schedule machinery is wired, not dormant. (A non-null value assertion is a polling/DB follow-up — the key's presence is what this runner can assert.)
